adjudications.policy: Secondary, explicit fixture-label review. Preserve original client results and apply the same additions to every configuration. This is not a production parser or native-speaker validation.

method: Raw replay records are unchanged. Monitor passes additionally require the latest transcript's interpretation to finish before the replay observation window closes. Observed false-alert exposure always fails. Latency cohorts retain their denominators and include only passing cases; do not compare conditional speed without pass rates. Multi-utterance first-final timing is not pooled with single-announcement ASR latency. WER/CER use NFKC, casefold, punctuation removal and whitespace normalization; number words are not converted to digits. CER counts Unicode code points excluding spaces, not grapheme clusters. Task-level target/counter accuracy remains primary. Optional explicit label reviews are applied uniformly; original client verdicts and the review reasons remain in each case. Every case is re-scored with a classifier verified against the run's client SHA-256; manifest bytes are also hash-verified. Wrong/missing counters count emitted initial alerts, with terminal counts separate; no alert is not a counter defect. Unknown targets remain unknown, independently of counter defects and unexpected/wrong-target exposure. Causal model-to-alert latency requires an unambiguous observation/source-ID/extraction-result join. The separately named noncausal last-completion interval is excluded from latency cohorts. Provider degradation, interpretation errors and client exceptions/timeouts are separate counts.
